question.text: Two cells $A$ and $B$ of emf $2 \mathrm{V}$ and $1.5 \mathrm{V}$ respectively, are connected as shown in figure through an external resistance $10 \Omega$ The internal resistance of each cell is $5 \Omega$. The potential difference $E_{A}$ and $E_{B}$ across the terminals of the cells $A$ and $B$ respectively are

solution.text: The figure can be redrawn as, The current through the circuit $$ \begin{aligned} i &=\frac{\text { net emf }}{\text { effective resistance }} \\ &=\frac{2-1.5}{5+5+10}=\frac{0.5}{20} \\ &=\frac{1}{40}=0.025 \mathrm{A} \end{aligned} $$ The terminal potential difference of the batteries and $$ \begin{aligned} V_{A} &=\varepsilon_{A}-i I_{A}=2-0.025 \times 5 \\ &=2-0.0125=1.875 \mathrm{V} \\ V_{B} &=\varepsilon_{B}+i I_{B} \end{aligned} $$ $$ =1.5+0.025 \times 5 $$ $$ =1,5+0.0125=1.625 \mathrm{V} $$
